clue.text: Offering of gifts? Now one's brought in a lot

parts.note: now, the current time, is the present

indicators.note: something brought in is carried inside, so the numeral goes within the other piece

parts.note: a ton is a colloquial word for a lot, as in 'tons of time'
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A ceremony where gifts are handed over, with a crowd now arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts I (one) inside A TON (a lot), making ATION after PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal handing-over of gifts or awards is called a ceremony of this kind; the question mark marks the pun on 'present' as gift.

clue.text: Poet to promote family

parts.note: to push a product or cause is to promote it
kin means one's relatives or family

explanation.surface: A writer pushing the interests of their relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pushkin was the great Russian poet, author of Eugene Onegin.

clue.text: New beer served up in style

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up says the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A fresh beer brought to the table with some flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns N + ALE, read upwards in this down entry, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash or flair, a synonym of style in the sense of panache.

clue.text: Hide some movie clips easily

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'moviE CLIPS Easily'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to obscure or block it from view, a synonym of hide.

parts.note: to tip something is to suggest it, as a tip is a hint
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Hinting that the best piece of music is a Tchaikovsky overture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Tippett was an English composer of operas and the oratorio A Child of Our Time.

clue.text: Cocaine gets distributed in the main

explanation.surface: Drugs being smuggled by sea across the ocean.

clue.text: Carol to some extent exhibiting stable condition

explanation.surface: A Christmas song in part, describing life in a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is only the opening two lines of the carol, hence 'to some extent'; read literally, the words describe the infant's lowly state in the stable.
explanation.definitionFit: The words open a well-known Christmas carol, and they also describe a newborn lying in a feeding trough in a stable for want of proper bedding.

clue.text: See 7
Give voice about stable creature in seasonal song

parts.note: to wail is to give voice in a loud cry
an ass, a donkey, is the creature of the Nativity stable

explanation.surface: Singing out about the donkey in a Christmas song.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassail is a toast and the festive song sung while going house to house at Christmas.

clue.text: Position taken by US chap? It has no real effect

indicators.note: the position is taken up by the man, so his name follows it

parts.note: a place is a position
Bo is a crossword name for an American fellow, a pal

explanation.surface: An American man fills a vacancy, but achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bo is American slang for a pal or fellow, much used by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given in a drug trial works only by suggestion, with no medicinal action.

clue.text: Restriction certainly accepted by the old

indicators.note: one thing accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
OK means yes, certainly

explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' names the container; 'the old' points to the archaic article seen in mock-Tudor shop names.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke is a burden or constraint, as in the yoke of oppression.

clue.text: Visit involving priest in party

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the visit word wraps the clergy abbreviation

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A call that includes the vicar at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' names the container; 'Visit' reads as a noun but works as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bout of lively fun, a binge or a celebration.

clue.text: Expert in a third of basic education?

explanation.surface: A specialist in one of the three Rs.
explanation.walkthrough: Basic schooling is the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic), so one R is a third of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for someone outstanding at something; and one R of the three Rs is a third of elementary schooling.

clue.text: Meat recipe forgotten in hurry

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so the recipe letter drops away

parts.note: to streak is to rush along, to hurry
R stands for recipe, the Latin 'take' heading a prescription

explanation.surface: A cook in such a rush that the meat recipe went out of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgotten' removes R (recipe) from STREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak is a thick slice of beef or other meat.

clue.text: Point of revolution mostly upheld second principle

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an axis is the line a spinning body revolves about

indicators.note: upheld, in a down clue, says the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A guiding principle for turning, mostly backed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts AXIS to AXI; 'upheld' turns MO into OM.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth taken as a starting rule.

clue.text: North American almost captured girl

indicators.note: almost means nearly whole, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: netted means caught, captured

explanation.surface: A girl nearly caught by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NETTED to NETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a female first name, as in the musical No, No, Nanette.

clue.text: Form of transport Bill's used to carry football team about

indicators.note: to carry is to hold inside, so the bill word contains the others

a football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
about gives CA

explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' names the container; 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a restaurant bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxicab is a hired car, a vehicle for getting about town.

clue.text: Traveller's in capital of Morocco, I allow

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so the first letter of the country is taken

parts.note: to grant is to allow

explanation.surface: A visitor in Rabat granting permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests Rabat, but it means the first letter, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is a person or animal on the move from one region to another.

clue.text: Retreating dog nipped by pig, a huge creature

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
something nipped is caught in a pincer grip, held within

parts.note: a hog is a pig
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A dog in retreat, bitten by a pig and some giant beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipped by' sets the follower inside the pig, and 'Retreating' then reads the whole combination backwards, not just the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the Philistine giant slain by David, so any giant thing is named after him.

clue.text: Article no good when camping? It's not directly relevant

indicators.note: with camping, 'when' sets the letters in the place a camper sleeps

parts.note: camping suggests being under canvas, inside a tent
a is the indefinite article

explanation.walkthrough: 'when' with 'camping' places the letters under canvas: someone camping is inside their shelter, so the article and the no-good abbreviation sit within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a digression that only touches the subject, as in going off at a tangent.

clue.text: Concern involving most of actors' body

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the concern word wraps the rest

parts.note: care means concern, worry

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: a cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the actors' word by its last letter, and 'involving' sets what is left inside the concern word.

clue.text: Nothing's recalled in seasonal lunacy

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Christmas madness is forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seasonaL LUNacy' holds LLUN; 'recalled' reads it backwards; the definition 'Nothing's' stands for 'Nothing is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Null means zero or void, amounting to nil.

clue.text: View historic resident of Britain

explanation.surface: A take on an early Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a point of view on something; the Angles were a Germanic people who settled in Britain after the Romans left.

clue.text: Field of activity that may be brought back for a time

indicators.note: brought back means turned the other way, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses A ERA, which spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a sphere or domain of work or study.

clue.text: I'm upset about silver-one of them brought gold

definitions.note: the definition describes the group, one of whom carried gold, so it points to a plural

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned letters enclose the metal
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written, I and M
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Distressed about silver, though one of the visitors came with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the clue's I'm and 'about' wraps that round the metal symbol. The definition refers to the whole group, one member of which bore gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men from the East bore gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Heads for your usual lovely English Christmas

explanation.surface: Wishing you the customary lovely English festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Yule is the old name for the Christmas season, as in yule log.

clue.text: Put out, English chap worried

explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to give out or issue, as light or smells do.

clue.text: Bravery of my squad, say, held in prison

belonging to me and my team is ours, the word our

explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' names the container; 'say' marks the possessive as one example of how my squad's things are described.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is boldness in the face of danger.

clue.text: It's premature in the present situation

definitions.text: It's premature in the present situation

parts.words: It's premature in the present situation
parts.note: the day before the gift-giving comes too early for presents, which are not opened yet; 'present' means gift, not now
